Music 0.2.2 fixes audio conversion failing when FFmpeg or ffprobe is missing.

- Automatically downloads missing conversion tools on Linux and Windows x86-64 when audio needs converting. Existing tools on PATH are preferred.
- Verifies pinned downloads with SHA-256 and caches them under `plugins/music/tools/` for offline reuse. No pip commands, administrator access or system PATH changes are needed.
- Runs installation on the existing background conversion worker, with cancellation, partial-download cleanup and retries. Server startup does not wait for downloads.
- Preserves uploads, existing packs and metadata if tool installation fails.

Stop the server, replace the previous Music wheel in `plugins/` with `endstone_music-0.2.2-py3-none-any.whl`, and restart. Keep only one Music wheel and preserve the existing Music data folder. Run `/cmusic generate` to convert uploads. The first conversion needs HTTPS access to GitHub if the tools are missing; later conversions reuse the verified cache. See INSTALL.md for offline setup.

Compatibility remains Endstone 0.11.15, BDS 1.26.60.6 / runtime 26.60 / protocol 2225 and Python 3.11+.

Local Windows validation: 109 tests, with 107 passing and two existing symlink checks skipped. Real first-time downloads and stereo/mono Vorbis conversion passed, including offline conversion from the built wheel using cached tools. The release workflow reruns the full suite on Linux. Live server integration and audible Bedrock-client playback remain unverified.
